findings.problem: Reuses the line "I think this one hurts" word for word from Prep stop 2, card 12 ("I think this one hurts, friend."), and also breaks the rule that he can say only once in a passage that a part is heavy (also said in stop 2, card 13).

Calls Naomi's words "praying" ("She's praying for good things for both of them"), which breaks "Call things what the text calls them" — Ruth 1:8-9 says "Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law... May the LORD enable each of you to find rest...".

Says "She's asking the LORD to bless each of them", which breaks the explicit example in papa-dorin.md under "Call things what the text calls them": ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'"

Quote cuts off before the end of the sentence without showing "…": Ruth 1:13 says "would you wait for them to grow up?", which is the second half of a sentence starting in 1:12 ("Even if I thought..., would you wait..."). Also adds a reason the text doesn't state ("She wants them to see how things really stand before they decide").
Quote starts mid-sentence without "…" ("would you wait for them to grow up?" is the continuation of the sentence from Ruth 1:12).

States "These are the words of a woman in deep sorrow" as a fact rather than marking the feeling as his own with "I think" or "I bet".
